b: v0.32.0 — MCP stream recovery, per-channel cost metrics, cron credential scoping # This release hardens two long-standing operational pain points (MCP transport drops mid-session, cron jobs inheriting wrong credentials) and adds the per-channel token/model metrics needed for downstream cost attribution. Features # Agent: stream_closed auto-recovery with circuit breaker. When an external MCP server disconnects mid-turn, the SDK's shared transport pool tears down, causing all in-process slaude_* tool calls to fail with "Stream closed". Previously this silently orphaned the turn. Now AgentManager detects the error in the tool_use_result , defers action to turn-end, and automatically reloads the session — injecting a synthetic "The MCP stream was restored. Please continue where you left off." prompt so the resumed session picks up without human input. A per-session circuit breaker (max 2 auto-reloads) prevents infinite reload loops; on the third consecutive failure the circuit opens and posts a visible error via the Bolt WebClient (bypassing the broken MCP surface). See src/agent/manager.ts . Metrics: per-channel token and model labels. Token counters ( slaude_tokens_total ) now carry channel_id and model labels on every increment, enabling downstream Prometheus queries to break cost by channel and by model. Previously all increments were label-less, making channel-level cost attribution impossible. See findings doc . Cron: private-MCP credential scoping by initiator. Cron jobs created inside a /1on1 session previously inherited the wrong MCP credentials at runtime — the live lock's config dir was used instead of the initiator's. resolveEffectiveIdentity() now unifies both code paths (config-dir selection and MCP credential scoping) through a single lookup keyed to the cron initiator. See findings doc and PR #66. Fixes # Metrics: model label derived from modelUsage keys. The SDKResultMessage type has no .model field; the prior code always resolved undefined . Fix derives the model name from Object.keys(modelUsage)[0] which reflects the actual model used. (#67 NIT) Metrics: row reference error in #fanout . The per-channel label fix accidentally used row.slack_channel_id directly inside #fanout , where row is not in scope. Corrected to Sessions.findById(sessionId)?.slack_channel_id . ( 3d8c77a ) Internal # Tests: stream_closed recovery coverage. Four new cases in manager-lifecycle.test.ts : happy-path auto-reload + auto-continue, circuit breaker (opens at attempt 3), array-format content block detection, and abort() mid-turn clearing pending state. ( 7854b87 ) Tests: cron private-MCP scoping. New cron-private-mcp-scoping.test.ts covering the identity resolution paths for both live-lock and initiator-based credential selection. b: v0.30.0 — channel-scoped souls, a remote brain process, and agent-as-itself on Slack # This release widens how a single deploy adapts to its surroundings. The soul can now speak differently per channel, the brain (KB engine) can run as its own OAuth-protected process instead of in-line, the agent can post on Slack as its own user account rather than the app bot, and cron jobs gained a real lifecycle. All four are opt-in and default to the prior behavior — existing deploys are unchanged. Features # Soul: channel-specific mandate & approvers (#62). SOUL.md can now carry per-channel ## Channel <#Cxxx> blocks, each with its own ### Mandate and ### Approvers . A new effectiveSoulForChannel resolver applies them with replace semantics — inside an overridden channel the channel's approver list is the only approver source for the approval gate and approver-based admin auth, and the channel mandate is injected as an authoritative <channel-mandate> directive that supersedes the global one. The grounding check extends to channel ids and per-channel approver ids, so the extractor can't widen the allowlist. Crucially, manager/backup are always retained as catchall approvers in every channel — a channel block can add approvers but never lock the operator out. Any resolution failure falls back to the global view so the gates never break. See docs/findings/2026-06-20-channel-soul-overrides.md . Brain: gbrain as a configurable remote OAuth MCP process (#61). The KB engine behind slaude_kb can now run as a separate, OAuth-protected MCP process, selected with SLAUDE_BRAIN_MODE=local|remote (default local — identical to the historical in-process brain). A BrainBackend seam routes brainCall / brainAdminCall to a LocalBackend (in-process) or a RemoteBackend (an OAuth'd MCP client to slaude brain-server ). Scope resolution and write-gating stay in slaude; the remote server is a dumb engine exposing two tools ( brain_op / brain_admin_op ). Auth is a Keycloak-first JWT resource-guard (jose JWKS, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata), fail-closed when issuer/audience are unset, with slaude brain connect reusing the shared OAuth loopback. See docs/findings/2026-06-20-brain-remote-mcp.md . Slack: opt-in post-as-user via xoxp token (#11). With SLACK_POST_AS_USER=true (plus an existing SLACK_USER_TOKEN ), the agent's replies/edits/reactions/uploads go out as its own real Slack account instead of the app bot — so a deploy no longer maintains two visible identities. The bot token stays for Socket Mode events and gate interactivity. Default off; existing deploys that set SLACK_USER_TOKEN for presence only are unchanged. Guards the self-echo loop that real-user posts (no bot_id ) would otherwise cause. See docs/findings/2026-06-09-post-as-slack-user.md . Cron: pause/resume/edit lifecycle (#50). Scheduled jobs gained a real lifecycle — /cron pause|resume|edit (and /cron-* aliases) plus runtime MCP tools ( pause_cron_job / resume_cron_job / edit_cron_job ). A paused state is honored by the scheduler (paused jobs skip unless manually queued), and lifecycle actions accept short id prefixes. Previously a job could only be created, listed, or removed — changing one meant delete-and-recreate. See docs/findings/2026-06-08-cron-on-channel.md . Internal # Coverage closed on the new surfaces: channel-override fixture emission + resolver fallback, post-as-user self-echo / auth-failure / warn branches, and the remote brain server's OAuth-guard JWKS path + boot/default-deps. The brain-server CLI bootstrap was extracted to its own entrypoint and codecov-ignored (process entrypoints are smoke-tested, not unit-tested), consistent with the existing project-level integration-only rationale. Full suite 1225 pass / 0 fail , tsc --noEmit clean, coverage 98.76%. b: v0.29.0 — Session self-awareness, agent-driven modes, and quieter Slack # A batch focused on the agent knowing and steering its own engagement state, plus two Slack-surface fixes. The model can now see when it's in a private /1on1 , learns about out-of-band state changes (connect/disconnect, model, mode, soul, cron) as they happen, and can start/release /1on1 and a new mention-only mode itself. Features # Session awareness in the system prompt + timeline (#54). The model had no idea what mode it was in. Now: a <session-mode> block names the locked user when a thread is /1on1 -locked (recomputed on the reboot /1on1 triggers — the system prompt is sent per-request, not frozen in the resumed transcript). And gate commands that run out-of-band of the model now drop a one-time marker into the next turn's context so the agent stays aware: /mcp connect / disconnect , /model , /mode , /soul , /cron-add / -remove . Delivered exactly once via a UserPromptSubmit hook; never spawns a model run. slaude_1on1 agent tool (#57). /1on1 was human-only. The agent can now start or release a 1on1 itself ( mcp__slaude_surface__set_one_on_one ) when a user asks to go private — same engine as the slash command, locked to the current speaker, no gating. Mounted in the slaude_surface family. Mention-only mode (#59). A new per-thread posture: /mention-only [off] (or the agent-facing mcp__slaude_surface__set_mention_only ) makes the agent reply only to messages that @-mention it and ignore plain follow-ups — like disengage, but persistent and conditional on a mention. Plain messages are recorded-suppressed if a session exists (context for when next tagged), else dropped. No gating. Fixes # /unignore* deadlock (#56). The ignore gate dropped messages before slash parsing, so a thread-ignore swallowed the very /unignore-thread meant to lift it — the thread was stuck ignored forever. /unignore* now bypasses the ignore gate (the blocklist + channel-mode + 1on1 gates after it still apply). The old test masked this by not thread-pinning its sends. Compact Slack links (#58). Agent-emitted bare URLs rendered as full raw URLs and ate whole lines. mdToMrkdwn now rewrites a standalone bare http(s) URL to a labeled <url|host> link — compact visible text, full URL preserved as the target. Markdown links, mrkdwn links, and autolinks are left untouched. Internal / Deprecations # /ingest soft-deprecated (#55). Superseded by brain memoize (gbrain captures knowledge automatically). The command now replies a deprecation notice and no longer runs; dropped from /help ; knowledge/ingest.ts + db/ingest-jobs.ts marked @deprecated . Code + kb_ingest_jobs table kept — full removal is a follow-up. New mention_only_threads table; set_one_on_one / set_mention_only folded into the slaude_surface tool family (no standalone servers). Full suite 1147 pass. b: v0.28.0 — MCP OAuth loopback: a public redirect_uri, so it works in k8s # v0.27.0 shipped the shared always-on OAuth loopback, but it could only ever advertise http://localhost:<port>/callback as its redirect_uri . In-cluster that's a dead end: the IdP redirects the user's browser , which then lands on their own localhost — not the pod. So behind an ingress the loopback never auto-completed and paste-back stayed the only working path. This release closes that gap. Features # MCP OAuth: public redirect_uri for the shared loopback. SharedLoopback gains a publicUrl option; register() now emits <publicUrl><callbackPath> (trailing slashes normalized) when set, falling back to the bound http://localhost:<port> otherwise. The listener still binds on a private port exactly as before — an ingress fronts publicUrl and forwards /callback back to it, where the signed- state demux is unchanged. Token exchange reuses the same flow.redirectUri , so the authorize and exchange legs stay consistent (an OAuth requirement). Wired via new env SLAUDE_OAUTH_PUBLIC_URL (trimmed; empty → localhost fallback), threaded into the singleton loopback at server boot. To switch a deployment from paste-back to loopback auto-complete: set SLAUDE_OAUTH_PUBLIC_URL=https://<host> and unset SLAUDE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URL (the latter takes priority in runConnect while set). h.t: v0.27.0 — MCP OAuth connect: one engine, two front doors, Slack-safe

b: v0.27.0 — MCP OAuth connect: one engine, two front doors, Slack-safe # This release reworks how the agent connects OAuth-backed MCP servers. The old /mcp connect flow had Slack hard-coded into it and a fresh per-flow loopback listener; the markdown→mrkdwn converter quietly corrupted the authorize URL. All three are fixed, and the agent can now connect a service from natural language — without ever weakening the security model: the authorize URL never passes through the LLM, no paste is needed, and every flow tears down cleanly. See docs/findings/2026-06-19-shared-oauth-loopback-surface-connect.md for the full investigation (including why the runtime synthesizes the OAuth tools the server never ships, and why exact-match redirect_uri + open dynamic registration makes a single shared callback port work). Features # MCP OAuth: shared always-on loopback, demuxed by signed state. A single callback listener (fixed port, default 3118) serves every session's OAuth callback, routing each by an HMAC-signed state that carries the session id (RFC 6749's client-set, echoed-back slot). Many sessions can authorize concurrently behind one pre-mapped port, instead of a fresh ephemeral listener per connect. Opt-in via SLAUDE_OAUTH_SHARED_LOOPBACK (+ _PORT , SLAUDE_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET ); the per-flow path remains the default. New modules in src/agent/mcp-oauth/ : state.ts , shared-loopback.ts , shared-client.ts , token-exchange.ts . MCP OAuth: natural-language connect. A new agent-facing tool mcp__slaude_connect__connect_mcp(server) lets the agent connect a service when a user asks ("connect workbench"). It routes into the same deterministic connectServer engine as /mcp connect — scope-gated (you connect your own services in a /1on1 ; the agent's shared identity is manager-only), fire-and-forget, returning only a status line. The authorize URL is posted out-of-band by the gateway and the loopback captures the result, so the model never sees the link and the user never pastes anything. Surface-aware connect. /mcp connect (loopback, paste-back, and button) now posts through the session's Surface instead of a hard-coded Slack client — channel-agnostic (Slack, sim, future surfaces), and it runs even outside a live turn. Fixes # Slack mrkdwn: emphasis flanking. The converter did a pure ** → * swap that Slack's renderer rejects. ***x*** → _*x*_ (Slack nests bold+italic, has no triple-star), ** x ** → *x* (inner padding trimmed — Slack won't emphasize with a space hugging the marker). Intra-word bold ( word**b**word ) is a Slack-renderer limit, left as-is. Slack mrkdwn: URLs corrupted by emphasis rules. Base64url query params (OAuth code_challenge / state ) contain __ , so a posted authorize URL got rewritten mid-string. mdToMrkdwn now carves <…> autolinks and bare http(s):// tokens (protect + restore, like code spans) before the link rule — fixing any agent-emitted URL, not just OAuth. Security # Auth-URL redaction on teardown. Once a connect flow settles — success, failure, or loopback timeout — the authorize-URL message is edited in place to strip the live link (redact, not delete), so no stale clickable secret lingers in the thread. State HMAC verified before routing. The shared loopback verifies the inbound state 's HMAC before registry lookup (wired to verifyState ), so a tampered/forged state is rejected before it can match a pending flow — closing a latent forgery surface flagged in security review. Synthesized OAuth tools denied. The permission gate hard-denies mcp__*__authenticate / __complete_authentication (the runtime/SDK-synthesized tools that use an uncontrolled redirect and would launder the URL through the model) — before the approval prompt, so they can't run and aren't even offered. Every connect is forced through our engine. Internal # New test suites: tests/mcp-oauth/ (state, shared-loopback, shared-client), tests/connect-mcp.test.ts , plus expanded gateway/permission-gate/format

b: v0.26.1 — approval gate auto-denies instead of hanging the MCP server # A patch release fixing a stream_closed cascade caused by approval gates that waited forever for a human click. Fixes # Approval: default to a 300s timeout when the soul config is 0 /unset. In-process MCP tool handlers that block too long trip the SDK's internal MCP timeout, which breaks not just the blocked call but every subsequent call on the same server (observed cascade: kb_memoize → reply , kb_search , list_kbs all fail with stream_closed ). The dominant trigger is kb_memoize 's implicit approval gate: approvalTimeoutSeconds defaults to 0 (wait forever) in SoulDataSchema , and most deployed personas never set it, so a gate with no clicker would hang indefinitely. The gate now falls back to 300s ( soulData().approvalTimeoutSeconds || 300 in src/gateway/core/gateway.ts ), after which the request cleanly resolves to approved: false — no cascade. An explicit approvalTimeoutSeconds in SOUL.md still overrides the default; the only behavior removed is unbounded "wait forever" ( 0 ), which was the bug. Approval: the Slack card now shows when it auto-denies. The Block Kit approval card renders a context line — ⏳ Auto-denies in *300s* if no one clicks. — using the live timeout value, so approvers know the gate is bounded ( src/gateway/slack/approval-gate.ts ). h.t: v0.26.0 — disengaged threads stay in-session via a suppress hook

b: v0.26.0 — disengaged threads stay in-session via a suppress hook # A feature release that changes how a disengaged thread is handled: instead of dropping every message after a user turns to a colleague and reconstructing the gap on re- @mention , the gap is now kept inside the session as real conversation history. The model simply doesn't respond while disengaged. Full writeup: 2026-06-16 reengage-hook-suppress . Features # Engagement: keep disengaged threads in-session, suppress the reply. Previously the gateway gate dropped every plain message after a thread disengaged (a user @mentions a colleague), so on re- @mention the agent resumed blind to everything said in the gap. The earlier approach rebuilt that gap by re-fetching the thread from Slack and injecting a synthetic preamble — heavy: a Slack round-trip, name resolution, recency caps, a truncation story. This release retains the gap instead of reconstructing it. Disengaged messages now flow into the session so the transcript stays continuously populated, and a UserPromptSubmit hook stops the model from responding while disengaged. On re-engage there is nothing to backfill — the context is already there. ( src/agent/manager.ts , src/gateway/core/gateway.ts ) The load-bearing detail: continue:false , not decision:"block" . A spike against the pinned SDK settled which hook return achieves "persist but don't process": decision:"block" discards the prompt before it is written to the transcript (no jsonl line), so the gap would be lost. continue:false enqueues and persists the user turn, then halts before generation — exactly "session stays populated, model never processes it", at ~0 output tokens. disengagedHookDecision(row) is pure and exported; the hook reads the session row live via Sessions.findById , so a re- @mention takes effect on the very next message. A colleague-mention in a thread with no session is still dropped — slaude never spins one up for an unrelated thread. Internal # suppress routing. b: v0.25.1 — status line never leaks secrets or filesystem paths # A patch release hardening the live "is thinking…" Slack status indicator ( assistant.threads.setStatus ) against leaking sensitive data. Fixes # Gateway: the status line no longer mirrors raw tool arguments. The status renderer inlined tool input — the Bash branch showed the first 50 chars of the command — so a secret on the command line ( curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …" , TOKEN=… cmd ) leaked into the broadcast status, and absolute paths in commands/args exposed filesystem structure outside the workspace. The renderer is extracted to src/gateway/core/status-text.ts and made safe by construction (fully deterministic — switch / string ops / regex, no model): Bash → verb + program name only ( running \ curl``); args are never emitted. The primary guarantee is structural — args/paths/queries are never rendered, so there is nothing to leak regardless of secret shape; redaction is a secondary net since regexes can miss novel formats. h.t: v0.25.0 — per-source gather: curated pages survive high-volume sources

b: v0.25.0 — per-source gather: curated pages survive high-volume sources # A feature release that fixes a retrieval-quality bug where a single curated page could be drowned out of the candidate set by a high-volume source. Full writeup: 2026-06-15 per-source-gather . Features # Knowledge: per-source candidate gather() . kb_search and kb_think previously pooled all allowed KB sources into one ranked candidate set, so a high-volume source — e.g. a bulk auto-generated corpus of thousands of near-empty model stubs — could monopolise the gather by sheer count. A small curated page never entered the pool, so the reranker never got to sort it up: a directory-style lookup resolved fine in a warm-context thread (the page was already in context) but failed in a cold thread ("the brain does not contain that data"). The new src/knowledge/gather.ts fans out one search per allowed source (single-source scope each), takes the top-K from each , then merges and re-ranks the union by the engine's own rerank_score . Every source — including small curated ones — is guaranteed candidate slots, so no source can crowd others out by volume; the reranker then sorts the empty stubs down and the curated page up. kb_search routes through gather() , and kb_think 's zero-citation cross-check uses it too, so an uncited-but-present page surfaces in search_fallback instead of more bulk-corpus noise. ( src/knowledge/gather.ts , src/knowledge/mcp-tools.ts ) Internal # gbrain stays stock — no fork. The fix only orchestrates the engine's existing search op differently; it does not patch the dependency. This is the proving ground — once validated in production, per-source ranking is intended for promotion upstream into gbrain itself. Failure posture is explicit. A single source failing drops to [] ; if every source fails the brain is genuinely down, so gather() rethrows and the handler maps it to an error rather than papering over a dead brain with empty results. Known limitation (follow-up). kb_think 's primary gather still runs inside the engine's runThink and is out of the wrapper's reach, so synthesis remains pooled; the per-source cross-check rescues the answer via search_fallback . Re-pointing the synthesis candidate step at the shared gather() is deferred as higher-risk. Tests # New tests/gather.test.ts — deterministic injected-call units (fan-out, flood-survival, dedup-by-slug, slugless-dedup, finalLimit + sort, score fallback, single-source fallback, partial-failure tolerated, total-failure rethrows) plus one self-contained real-engine smoke. tests/brain-mcp-tools.test.ts updated for the new kb_search contract. Patch coverage 100%. Docs # Added a public-repo working rule: never commit real names, organisation names, internal channel names, or internal service/source identifiers — use generic placeholders. Findings docs describe the mechanism, not deployment specifics.

b: v0.22.0 — KB-first means it, and a quieter resume # A small but pointed release: the knowledge-base directive moves from polite suggestion to runtime contract, and a scary-but-harmless warning stops leaking into Slack when an old session migrates onto resumable-sessions. Plus the design for actually enforcing KB-first, captured for a later build. Features # Soul: KB-first is now mandatory, not advisory. The RUNTIME_BASELINE KB-first stance was a self-judged conditional ("when you lack context… query the KB"), so a confident-but-wrong agent could answer straight from its training and the runtime never noticed. It's rewritten in the imperative register the approval gate uses: before any substantive answer or non-trivial action — and always before a mutation — the agent MUST query the KB first (default kb_search , or kb_think for a cited synthesis), must not answer from its own weights when brain tools are mounted ("your training is not this team's source of truth, the KB is"), and must state gaps explicitly instead of guessing. Pure chitchat / acknowledgement ("Hi", "thanks 👍") stays exempt. Lives in the non-overridable baseline, injected every turn. Fixes # Agent: the resume-miss warning no longer leaks to Slack. A session created before resumable-sessions has claude_started=1 but no CLI transcript under slaude's id, so its first boot resume-misses. That self-heals — #startSession clears the flag and reboots seeding --session-id , so the new claude conversation lands under slaude's id and later resumes hit. But the miss also arrived as a result(is_error) , which #fanout emitted unconditionally — so the user saw a :warning: error: No conversation found with session ID: … for an expected, already-handled condition. #fanout now suppresses only the resume-miss (shared RESUME_MISS_RE with the retry path), logging a [resume-attempt] line server-side instead; every other turn error still surfaces. One-time, now-invisible migration for pre-feature sessions. Internal # Docs: KB-first enforcement design. Follow-up to the wording hardening above — how to add a Stop-hook forcing function without nagging on "Hi". Tiered design (hard-enforce only on substantive-work-without- kb_* , trust prose for pure replies), shadow/metric-mode rollout, open questions. Designed, not implemented. See docs/findings/2026-06-13-kb-first-enforcement.md . A soul_override MCP surface tool exposes the same mutations to the agent, also manager-gated. Previously the trust/DM/block lists were frozen in SOUL.md and only changeable by editing the file and redeploying. See docs/findings/2026-06-11-soul-runtime-overrides.md . Baseline: upload file artifacts instead of paths. The runtime baseline now instructs the agent that when a tool produces a file (image, PDF, CSV, log dump, generated asset) it must upload the file itself via mcp__slaude_surface__upload rather than replying with a local path or an expiring URL — inline content survives link expiry, crosses networks, and renders in-thread.
